description: Denial of Service through Email Flooding Attackers can send a large volume of emails or API requests without any throttling mechanisms in place. This could overwhelm system resources and impact service availability. An attacker writes a script to continuously send emails through the system, depleting SES quotas and overwhelming the email processing pipeline.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement WAF with rate limiting rules
recommendation: Add SQS throttling and Lambda concurrency limits
recommendation: Implement API Gateway with usage plans

description: Insufficient Authentication and Authorization The system lacks proper authentication mechanisms, particularly for the admin panel and email services. No MFA requirement increases the risk of unauthorized access. An attacker gains access to the admin panel through weak credentials, allowing them to modify email configurations and access sensitive data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement IAM roles and policies
recommendation: Enable MFA for all users

description: Malware Distribution through Email Attachments Malicious files can be attached to emails without proper scanning, potentially delivering malware to recipients or storing dangerous content in S3. description: Insecure Data Storage and Access Controls Lack of proper access controls and encryption for stored emails could allow unauthorized access to sensitive data. An attacker exploits weak S3 bucket policies or IAM roles to access emails belonging to other users.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
